INDUSTRIAL ENGINEERING · FACILITY DESIGN

Pet Food Production Facility Design

Launching study and industrial design for a new brand of organic dog food and natural snacks.

Project overview

This project developed the launching study for a new brand focused on dog health through organic food and natural snacks. The target market included young women aged 18 to 25 who own dogs, as well as veterinarians in Chía and Bogotá.

A ten-year demand forecast was prepared using historical dog and cat food sales data from 2011 to 2016. The analysis considered an expected market share of 5% and used double exponential smoothing based on linear regression.

Planning and engineering activities

  • Demand Forecasting: Estimated demand over a ten-year horizon using historical market data.
  • Supplier Selection: Applied the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), considering price, transport, quality and availability.
  • Plant Location: Evaluated five location alternatives using a linear programming model to minimize distances between suppliers and customers. The selected location was on the Cota–Siberia road.
  • Production Planning: Defined production capacity and a weekly schedule based on machine capacity and monthly demand.
  • Process Design: Characterized the production process, consisting of nine stages for food and one additional stage for snacks.
  • Facility Design: Developed the plant layout and considered architectural, organizational, waste-management, hydraulic and electrical requirements.
  • Financial Study: Included a financial evaluation as part of the project feasibility study.

The project combined market analysis, operations research, production planning and facility design to develop an integrated proposal for the launch of the new product line.
